The *Ketakapupphiyattheraapadāna* is a verse text included in the Therāpadāna section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the past devotional deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder (thera) Ketakapupphiya. The SuttaCentral database catalogs the poem under the reference Tha Ap 516 and records five translations into modern languages [SuttaCentral].

No direct external parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are recorded on SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, automated text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal connections across 34 texts with 96 matching passages, reflecting the recurring formulaic idiom typical of the collection [DharmaNexus]. Its verses share notable alignments with the first volume of the commentary on the Theragāthā (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*), as well as significant segment-level parallels (particularly spanning §§2–8) with adjacent and related botanical-offering narratives in the Therāpadāna, such as the *Nāgapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 517), *Kuṭajapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 519), and *Paṭṭipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 461) [DharmaNexus].
